Searchings
SURCH-ings
n. pl. (searchings of heart; inward examinations, self-questionings)
From search, Old French cerchier, from Latin circare, to go about or round. The Hebrew cheqer means a searching out or investigation, from chaqar, to dig into.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

In the roll-call of Deborah's song, Reuben is twice mentioned and twice found wanting: “Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart” (Judges 5:16). Searchings of heart are inward examinations, deep self-questionings. The verse before had used a kindred phrase: “For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts of heart” (Judges 5:15). Reuben debated. The tribe held councils, weighed the matter, examined motives, and did not come. Deborah sets that against Zebulun and Naphtali, who jeoparded their lives unto the death. The searchings were real and may well have been sincere; they were also, in the event, a substitute for obedience. Scripture elsewhere commends the searching of the heart in the strongest terms — “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts” (Psalm 139:23) — but notice who does the searching there. Self-examination offered to God issues in action; self-examination held among the sheepfolds issues in deliberation that never ends.

Jdg 5:16 — "Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart."

Jdg 5:15 — "And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; even Issachar, and also Barak: he was sent on foot into the valley. For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts of heart."

Psa 139:23 — "Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:"

Modern Corruption

Endless introspection takes the place of obedience, and the examining of motives becomes the respectable reason for never acting.

expand to see more

Deborah's line about Reuben is one of the quietest rebukes in Scripture and one of the most searching. The tribe did not refuse in defiance; it deliberated. Great searchings of heart, and no men at Kishon. A therapeutic age multiplies exactly this failure, teaching believers to process their feelings about a duty rather than to do it, and dignifying the delay as discernment.

Self-examination is commanded: examine yourselves whether ye be in the faith, and let a man examine himself before eating of that bread. But the Psalmist's pattern turns the work outward and upward, asking God to search him, and ending in a prayer to be led in the way everlasting. Searching that ends in the self ends nowhere. The test of true searching of heart is whether a man goes down to the battle when the LORD's call comes.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

From search, Latin circare; Hebrew cheqer, a searching out; Judges 5:16 marks Reuben's great searchings of heart.

expand to see more

Latin circare, to go about, through Old French cerchier: to search.

Hebrew cheqer, a searching out, from chaqar, to dig into.

Judges 5:16 is the only occurrence of searchings in the Authorized Version.

Verse 15 uses the kindred phrase great thoughts of heart.

Psalm 139:23 asks God to do the searching and ends in a prayer to be led.
